learning: If the shorter lead cuts max_error and oscillation while holding progress, the lead direction is confirmed and the next step is a further shortening or sensor_size 0.012. If line loss rises or progress falls, y=0.05 remains the optimum for this controller.
notes: Iteration 4 controller and layout, with only the forward sensor row moved from y=0.05 to y=0.03 m, as the Builder requested. The controller is held at iteration 4 values so the race isolates the lead change.
rationale: Evidence: iteration 4 (wheel_track 0.08 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, mass 0.8 kg, seven 16 mm sensors at y=0.05 m, kp 1.35, kd 0.25, ki 0.02) is the best design at 58.54. Every run ends off_track with max_error on the 0.06 m floor, and line loss is now rare (oval 0, s-bend about 0.95, slalom about 0.85). Iterations 5 and 6 showed that a larger wheel_radius (41.4) and a heavier mass (42.7) both cut s-bend progress, and iteration 7 (wheel_radius 0.025 m) scored 57.92, so the speed and inertia optimum sits near the iteration 4 values. The only change in this geometry is the forward sensor position, moved from y=0.05 to y=0.03 m, as the Builder requested. The sensor lead does not enter the controller equations, so the controller stays identical to iteration 4. That keeps the race isolating the geometry change. The signal weights are still proportional to sensor x, and last_direction line-loss recovery is unchanged. I expect progress near or above 0.185 on the s-bend, with max_error and steering_oscillation at or below iteration 4. The risk is a shorter lead that adds lag and more line loss on the sharpest bends. I make no outcome claim for this candidate.
